Inquest opened into death of man at Silloth golf course

4 hrs ago
Court
Cumbria
By Darren Shield Reporter

Share

0 comments
Read More

motorists caught using mobile phones
Silloth Golf Course lies next to the Solway Coast (Image: Gary Lisbon/Silloth on Solway)

0:00 / 1:27
Instaread

An inquest has been opened into the death of a 61-year-old man who was found unresponsive at a golf course in Cumbria.

Michael Westgate, of Blitterlees, Silloth, died on September 16, 2026, at the grounds of Silloth-on Solway Golf Club

The inquest opening, held by Area Coroner for Cumbria Margaret Taylor at the Coroner's Court in Workington, heard that Mr Westgate, who was born on March 29, 1965, was widowed at the time of his death.

A provisional medical cause of death was given as haemorrhagic shock caused by incised wounds.

Ms Taylor said: "An investigation into Mr Westgate's death has been required because he died from self-inflicted wounds."

Mr Westgate was identified by Detective Chief Inspector Patrick McDonnell, who has also provided a statement to the coroner outlining the circumstances in which he was discovered.

Ms Taylor has requested a factual statement from Silloth Group Practice, with particular reference to Mr Westgate's mental health.

Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear NHS Foundation Trust has also been asked to establish whether he was known to its services and, if so, to provide records covering his final three months.

A pen portrait of Mr Westgate's life has been requested from his family.

Ms Taylor indicated that the case may be suitable for an inquest conducted in writing, depending on the evidence received.

A full inquest has been provisionally listed for December 15, 2026, subject to all the required information being available.
